questions.text: A student is asked to maximize the area of a rectangle with perimeter 40 and writes $A = 40$. What went wrong?
options: They set the quantity to optimize equal to the constraint value
questions.explain: The perimeter is 40 (constraint). The area is the thing to maximize, and it is a function, not a number.

questions.text: In an optimization problem, the quantity being optimized is always an area or a volume.
questions.explain: It can be a cost, a time, a distance, a profit, even a slope.

questions.text: Before you differentiate, the function you are optimizing should be written with only **one** variable.
questions.explain: The constraint lets you replace one variable, so the function has a single variable and an ordinary derivative.
